featured_reviews.name: Perpetual Gomes
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Slow in Kandivli recently with my cousin sister, and honestly, while the food and coffee were good, the overall experience and service left us extremely uncomfortable.

When we entered, there were multiple empty 4-seater tables available (which remained empty throughout most of our visit), yet we were seated at their “community table”  which is essentially a tiny circular table against the wall that is genuinely not practical for two people ordering food and drinks.

One of the waiters later moved us to a proper table after realizing the issue, but shortly after, someone managing the cafe asked the waiter to move us back to the tiny community table again. We even mentioned that it would be difficult to comfortably eat there once food arrived, but were told “it will be fine.”

Unfortunately, it really wasn’t.

Things kept falling while we were eating because there simply wasn’t enough space. We had to move the cutlery setup ourselves just to make room for the plates and drinks. Nobody checked in or offered any solution despite clearly seeing the inconvenience.

What honestly made the experience worse was noticing another individual sitting alone with camera equipment/content setup being comfortably given a larger table while we, as paying customers ordering food and coffee, were repeatedly denied one despite tables remaining vacant throughout our meal.

If the cafe had been full, this would’ve been understandable. But it wasn’t.

The food itself was genuinely good and reasonably priced, which makes this more disappointing because the experience could have been great with just basic consideration and hospitality.

Also adding a service charge after this experience honestly felt a little absurd.

I hope the cafe improves how they treat regular customers moving forward because good food alone isn’t enough to make people return.

featured_reviews.name: Megha Solanki
featured_reviews.review_text: This café is a hidden gem with cosy vibes and a welcoming atmosphere. The food exceeded expectations — the burrito bowl had an authentic Mexican flavor that felt truly international. Pairing it with a Vietnamese iced latte was a delightful choice, and the tiramisu French toast was indulgent yet balanced. The menu shows creativity while staying true to global tastes, making it a perfect spot for anyone who enjoys exploring diverse cuisines. featured_reviews.name: Pragya Singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
TLDR: Good ambience, (at best) average Food, terrible beverages. Overpriced disappointment!

We were genuinely excited to visit the place and had already returned twice because of the waiting earlier but God were we disappointed! Biggest let down was the signature cold chocolate which was just a sugary syrup and a disgrace to be called 55% dark chocolate. It tasted like drinking sweet flour (probably to make it thicker). Felt so bad about the extra calories and 400 bucks going down the drain for this whereas a small sachet of Tiggle does a WAYYY better job at home. I even requested the server if I could get a stronger version of chocolate by tweaking it after having just one sip but he refused by saying that the jaggery/palm sugar already comes mixed with the chocolate so there's nothing they can do about it.
The burrito bowl was average, not bad but nothing I'd go again for. And the nachos were a bit stale, so much for "fresh and from scratch" ingredients.
The broccoli and cottage cheese burger didn't feel like it had any cottage cheese but rather just broccoli and mushed potatoes. The hand cut fries that came with it were too salty, oily and soggy.
Lastly, the spiced orange cream iced latte only sounded fancy and had cream chunks instead of a well frothed foam on top.
The only good parts were that the ambience has been tastefully decorated and the service is quick.

Also, I am a hardcore non-vegetarian and my review is primarily based on how my taste buds felt.

Below are the dishes we ordered:
🍔🍠🍟 Sweet potato spinach burger served with fries [3.8/5] - The burger was good, but I’ve had better veg burgers. The fries were crispy, good enough.
🥟🥘 Every morning dumpling [3/5] - Although this was considered a small plate/side the servig size was GOOD. But the taste was not expected. The dumplings were served in some gravy which had a very familiar taste with a lot of Indian spices. Unable to recall which home made curry did it reflect.

But beyond that it was okay.

featured_reviews.review_text:

featured_reviews.review_text:

Started with the coconut matcha. Honestly, it didn’t impress me. The taste wasn’t something I’d want to try again, and using what felt like a Paper Boat–style coconut base at that price point didn’t really match the expectation.

Ambience was decent, nothing too special. Service was a little slow, though it was quite crowded, so that might be understandable.

Overall, not a bad experience, just not as memorable as I expected

featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
A great restaurant is often remembered for a signature dish. An exceptional one is remembered for creating an experience where every element—from the food and drinks to the service and ambience—comes together seamlessly. The Backyard Brew in Versova does exactly that.
Set in a charming and inviting space, the restaurant instantly makes you want to settle in and stay awhile. The atmosphere is warm, relaxed, and effortlessly stylish, making it the perfect setting for everything from leisurely brunches to long dinners with friends and family.
The food is where The Backyard Brew truly shines. Among the standout dishes, the Chicken Ala Kiev deserves special mention—beautifully prepared, packed with flavour, and easily one of the highlights of the meal. Cutting into the perfectly crisp exterior reveals a succulent chicken filling that is rich, comforting, and expertly executed. The Fish & Chips was equally impressive, featuring perfectly crisp batter, flaky fish, and excellent accompaniments that elevated this classic comfort dish. Every plate reflected careful preparation, quality ingredients, and a kitchen that understands the importance of balancing flavour with presentation.
The beverage menu is equally noteworthy. The Matcha was smooth, earthy, and expertly crafted, while the milkshakes were rich, indulgent, and wonderfully satisfying without being overly sweet.
A special shoutout must go to their seasonal Mango Special Menu, which was nothing short of delightful. It’s refreshing to see a restaurant celebrate the king of fruits with such creativity and finesse. The Mango Cheesecake was luscious and beautifully balanced, allowing the natural sweetness of the fruit to shine. The Mango Pancakes were light, indulgent, and bursting with fresh mango flavour, while the Mango Milkshake proved to be the perfect seasonal treat. Every mango-inspired offering felt thoughtfully curated and beautifully executed.
Beyond the excellent food, the service deserves equal praise. The staff were attentive, knowledgeable, and genuinely welcoming throughout our visit. Recommendations were thoughtful, service was prompt, and there was a sincere warmth that made the experience feel personal rather than transactional.
What ultimately sets The Backyard Brew apart is its ability to combine culinary quality with genuine hospitality. In a city filled with dining options, it manages to create an experience that feels both memorable and comforting. You arrive expecting a good meal and leave already planning your next visit.
For anyone exploring Versova’s vibrant food scene, The Backyard Brew is an easy recommendation. Come for the ambience, stay for the exceptional food, don’t miss the Chicken Ala Kiev, Fish & Chips, Matcha, and milkshakes, and if you’re visiting during mango season, the Mango Special Menu is an absolute must-try.

featured_reviews.name: Rajinder Singh Puller
featured_reviews.review_text:
​A Solid Breakfast, But Still Searching for the "Wow" Factor

​After a rather underwhelming visit to The Backyard Brew a few years ago, I decided to return recently to meet a friend for breakfast. I wanted to give them another fair shot, especially given their reputation in the local coffee scene. Overall, while the experience was certainly an improvement over my last visit, I left with somewhat mixed feelings.

The hospitality was a high point. The staff members were attentive and patient, allowing me plenty of time to look over the menu without feeling rushed. It’s the kind of welcoming environment that makes for a pleasant morning catch-up.

I opted for the Eggs Benedict paired with a simple cappuccino.
​The Eggs: They were poached to perfection—the highlights of the meal.
​
While the hollandaise was tasty, it was just a notch short of being "amazing." It lacked that final punch of flavor to make it truly memorable.

​The coffee was my biggest point of contention. While the cappuccino was perfectly fine, I expected something spectacular from a place known for its brewing expertise. It was a standard cup, but it didn't stand out. In hindsight, I probably should have experimented with one of their more specialized blends.
​
The Backyard Brew is a reliable spot if you are already in the neighborhood. It is certainly "can-visit" material for a casual meal, but I wouldn't suggest traveling a long distance specifically for it. There isn't quite enough "magic" yet to justify a pilgrimage across town, but I might find myself back there eventually to see if they can finally bridge the gap from "good" to "great."

The other thing was that the juices turned out to be too expensive. That glass cost ₹450 without taxes. Nearly equivalent to a dish. That was too much. And for that size of glass ₹200 or ₹250 would have been good.

featured_reviews.name: Srishti Kadam
featured_reviews.review_text:
We had our breakfast buffet here while we were staying at this hotel and the food was super delicious, so we ate till our tummies were full.
The place is hygienic and the view is spectacular from the glass pane windows. Comfortable wooden chairs and tables with proper cutlery, give the vibe of a fine dining restaurant. Staff is extremely polite, well mannered and their service is pretty quick.
Coming to the food, we tasted most of the things available for buffet and we had no complaints. Absolutely loved the chicken sausages..🤤 We definitely had a great start to our day thanks to this amazing food experience..😋
